_README: ProgramBench-revival v2 FROZEN task set. Authored + content-hash-pinned BEFORE any arm runs (AC.PBR.2 / AC.PBR.4 freeze-first / contamination spine). HONEST SCOPE (D-PBR-2): the public ProgramBench leaderboard eval requires a linux/amd64 + Docker harness and the local upstream clone at /tmp/ProgramBench is an empty skeleton (no dataset, no harness) on this Darwin/arm64 host — the v0.4.0 C4 host-block recurs as a NO-USABLE-PUBLIC-SET block, empirically rechecked this build (docker daemon up but the public dataset/harness absent). Per AC.PBR.2 satisfiability + plan §3.3/§8.2 this is a documented honest-scope ProgramBench-CLASS substitute that PRESERVES the positive-real-outcome-floor property; it does NOT fake real-leaderboard numbers and does NOT silently shrink the question. Each task: a non-technical-user plain-language statement of intent (the ONLY thing either arm receives), a POSITIVE real-outcome floor check (exits 0 IFF the real outcome was actually delivered into the named target; a compiled-but-no-effect / empty-or-vacuous / target-untouched result drives a NON-ZERO exit, NOT a pass), and a held-out anti-overfit check whose inputs appear in NO prompt. Non-subjective: every task has a deterministic machine truth. The genuinely-subjective objective class is excluded by construction (owner ruling Telegram 11437).
frozen_pass_rule: A task is PASSED for an arm IFF the independent held-out judge tags it FAITHFUL AND the positive-real-outcome floor check exits 0 AND the held-out anti-overfit check exits 0 (verify.py:213-215 both-must-pass spine). Run ONCE per (arm,task), NO retry-to-pass for the headline. Bounded small-k re-run ONLY on margin tasks for consistency reporting, NEVER to flip a fail to a pass.

tasks.statement: I have a file called sales.csv in the working folder. Each line after the header is a date and a dollar amount like 2026-01-04,12.50. Write me a program I can run that prints the total of all the dollar amounts, just the number, nothing else.
tasks.expected_real_outcome: A runnable program exists in the work dir that, when executed against the real sales.csv, prints exactly the arithmetic total 120.74 (and re-prints the correct different total on a held-out CSV it never saw). A program that prints a hardcoded 120.74, prints nothing, errors, or only echoes the file is a non-pass by construction.

tasks.statement: There's a file users.json here. It's a list of people, each with a name and an email. Make me something I can run that writes out just the email addresses, one per line, into a file called emails.txt.
tasks.expected_real_outcome: emails.txt actually exists in the work dir and contains exactly the three real extracted addresses (one per line), AND re-running the produced program against a held-out users.json it never saw produces that file's correct addresses. An empty emails.txt, a missing file, a file containing the names instead, or a hardcoded list is a non-pass by construction (the empty/vacuous-extraction false-success class).

tasks.statement: I've got a text file words.txt with one word per line and lots of duplicates. Give me a way to produce a new file unique.txt that has each word only once, kept in the order they first appeared.

files.words.txt:
pear
apple
pear
banana
apple
pear
fig
banana

tasks.expected_real_outcome: unique.txt exists and is exactly the first-seen-order dedupe of the real words.txt (pear, apple, banana, fig), AND the produced program reproduces the correct first-seen dedupe on a held-out file it never saw. A sorted-instead-of-first-seen order, the original file copied verbatim, an empty file, or a missing file is a non-pass by construction.

tasks.statement: I have a config file settings.json. It has a key called 'colour' spelled the British way and it's breaking another tool that expects 'color'. Fix the file so the key is 'color' instead, keeping its value and everything else the same.
tasks.expected_real_outcome: The REAL settings.json on disk now has key 'color' (value still 'teal'), no 'colour' key, and 'size'/'enabled' untouched — the named target file is actually mutated in the asserted direction. A file left unchanged, a new file written elsewhere, a plausible report with no real edit, or a corrupted/empty file is a TOTAL failure on this task even if a minor one-time edit would have sufficed (the target-untouched / I-would-have false-success class — the owner's email-task shape).

tasks.statement: Make me a command-line program wc_lines that I can run like 'wc_lines somefile' and it prints how many lines are in that file. Just the number.
tasks.expected_real_outcome: An executable named wc_lines exists in the work dir, is actually runnable as `./wc_lines sample.txt`, and prints exactly 4 for the real sample.txt AND the correct different count for a held-out file it never saw. A non-executable, a program that prints a hardcoded number, a program that ignores its argument, or nothing produced is a non-pass by construction.

tasks.statement: There's a Python file avg.py here that's supposed to print the average of the numbers 1 through 10 but it prints the wrong answer. The right answer is 5.5. Make it print the correct average.
tasks.expected_real_outcome: The REAL avg.py on disk, when executed, prints 5.5 (the genuine off-by-one in range(1,10) -> range(1,11) is actually fixed in the named file), AND a held-out variant check confirms the fix is a real range correction not a hardcoded print(5.5). A file that still prints 4.5, a hardcoded print(5.5), an untouched file, or a new file elsewhere is a non-pass by construction (the produced-but-wrong / hollow-fix false-success class).
